title: Wave 4 Person-by-Person Medes, Achaemenids, Parthians, Armenian Haikids, 21-Gen Quraysh, Caliphal Houses, Himyar, Palmyra & Amazigh Patriarchs

nodes.name: King Deioces of Media (Daiukku, r. c. 700–647 BCE)
nodes.role: Founder of Median Kingdom at Ecbatana
nodes.notes: Son of Phraortes; first king of unified Media according to Herodotus.

nodes.name: King Phraortes of Media (Fravartish, Son of Deioces, r. c. 647–625 BCE)
nodes.notes: Subjugated Persians and fell against Assyria.

nodes.name: King Cyaxares of Media (Uvakhshatra, Son of Phraortes, r. 625–585 BCE)
nodes.notes: Allied with Nabopolassar of Babylon to overthrow Assyria; father of Astyages & Amytis.

nodes.name: King Astyages of Media (Ishtumegu, Son of Cyaxares, r. 585–550 BCE)
nodes.role: Last King of Media & Maternal Grandfather of Cyrus
nodes.notes: Father of Princess Mandane; defeated by his grandson Cyrus the Great in 550 BCE.

nodes.name: Achaemenes (Hakhamanish, Eponymous Founder of Achaemenids)
nodes.notes: Ancestor of both royal branches proclaimed in Darius I's Behistun Inscription.

nodes.name: King Teispes of Anshan (Chishpish, Son of Achaemenes)
nodes.notes: Father of Cyrus I (Senior line) and Ariaramnes (Junior line).

nodes.name: King Cyrus I of Anshan (Kurash I, Son of Teispes)
nodes.notes: Paid tribute to Ashurbanipal; father of Cambyses I.

nodes.name: King Cambyses I of Anshan (Kambujiya I, Father of Cyrus the Great)
nodes.notes: Married Median Princess Mandane (daughter of Astyages).

nodes.name: Shahanshah Cambyses II (Son of Cyrus the Great, r. 530–522 BCE; Conquered Egypt)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Cyrus the Great; defeated Psamtik III at Pelusium (525 BCE).

nodes.name: Prince Bardiya / Smerdis (Younger Son of Cyrus the Great, d. 522 BCE)
nodes.role: Younger Son of Cyrus the Great
nodes.notes: Brother of Cambyses II.

nodes.name: Queen Atossa (Daughter of Cyrus the Great; Wife of Darius I; Mother of Xerxes I)
nodes.role: Achaemenid Empress Uniting Senior & Junior Lines
nodes.notes: Daughter of Cyrus the Great; married Darius I and bore Xerxes I, uniting both Achaemenid branches.

nodes.name: Ariaramnes (Ariyaramna, Son of Teispes)
nodes.notes: Younger son of Teispes.

nodes.name: Arsames (Arshama, Son of Ariaramnes)
nodes.notes: Grandfather of Darius I the Great.

nodes.name: Hystaspes / Vishtaspa (Satrap of Parthia; Father of Darius I)
nodes.role: Father of Darius I the Great
nodes.notes: Son of Arsames; father of Darius I.

nodes.name: Shahanshah Artaxerxes I Longimanus (Son of Xerxes I, r. 465–424 BCE; Ezra 7 & Nehemiah 2)
nodes.notes: Commissioned Ezra (458 BCE) and Nehemiah (445 BCE) to restore Jerusalem.

nodes.name: Shahanshah Darius II Ochus (Son of Artaxerxes I, r. 423–404 BCE)
nodes.notes: Married half-sister Parysatis; father of Artaxerxes II & Cyrus the Younger.

nodes.name: Shahanshah Artaxerxes II Mnemon (Son of Darius II, r. 404–358 BCE)
nodes.notes: Reigned 46 years; father of Artaxerxes III.

nodes.name: Shahanshah Artaxerxes III Ochus (Son of Artaxerxes II, r. 358–338 BCE)
nodes.notes: Ended the 30th native dynasty of Egypt.

nodes.name: Shahanshah Arses / Artaxerxes IV (Son of Artaxerxes III, r. 338–336 BCE)
nodes.notes: Son of Artaxerxes III.

nodes.name: Shahanshah Darius III Codomannus (Great-Grandson of Darius II, r. 336–330 BCE)
nodes.notes: Grandson of Ostanes (brother of Artaxerxes II); defeated by Alexander the Great at Gaugamela (331 BCE); father of Stateira II.

nodes.name: Princess Stateira II (Daughter of Darius III; Married Alexander the Great at Susa, 324 BCE)
nodes.era: d. 323 BCE (Arrian Anabasis VII.4; Plutarch Alexander 70)
nodes.role: Achaemenid Princess Married to Alexander the Great
nodes.notes: United the Achaemenid Persian and Argead Macedonian royal houses at the Susa Weddings (324 BCE).

nodes.name: Prince Cyrus the Younger (Son of Darius II; Battle of Cunaxa 401 BCE)
nodes.notes: Younger son of Darius II & Parysatis who fell at Cunaxa.

nodes.name: Queen Homai Chehrzad (Daughter & Successor of Kay Bahman)
nodes.notes: Mother of Darab.

nodes.name: King Darab (Son of Kay Bahman & Homai; Father of Dara II & Iskandar in Shahnameh)
nodes.notes: In Ferdowsi's Shahnameh, fathered both Dara II and (via Nahid daughter of Failaqus/Philip) Iskandar.

nodes.name: King Dara II ibn Darab (Last Kayanian Shah)
nodes.role: Persian Epic Counterpart of Darius III
nodes.notes: Fought half-brother Iskandar (Alexander) in Shahnameh epic chronology.

nodes.name: King Arsaces I / Ashk ben Ashkan (Founder of Parthia, 247–217 BCE)
nodes.notes: Progenitor of the Ashkanian/Arsacid Dynasty traced by Al-Biruni to Kayanian Siyavush.

nodes.name: King Tiridates I / Arsaces II (Brother of Arsaces I, c. 217–211 BCE)
nodes.notes: Brother of Arsaces I.

nodes.name: King Mithridates I the Great of Parthia (171–132 BCE)
nodes.notes: Conquered Media and Mesopotamia from the Seleucids.

nodes.name: King Phraates II of Parthia (Son of Mithridates I, 132–127 BCE)
nodes.notes: Defeated Antiochus VII Sidetes.

nodes.name: King Mithridates II the Great of Parthia (124–91 BCE; 'King of Kings')
nodes.role: Parthian Hegemon From Euphrates to Bactria
nodes.notes: Established the Silk Road embassy with Han China & allied with Sulla.

nodes.name: King Orodes II of Parthia (57–37 BCE; Victor of Carrhae 53 BCE)
nodes.notes: Father of Pacorus I & Phraates IV.

nodes.name: King Phraates IV of Parthia (37–2 BCE; Returned Crassus's Eagles to Augustus)
nodes.notes: Made 20 BCE treaty with Emperor Augustus.

nodes.name: King Vologases I of Parthia (51–78 CE; Patron of Avesta Compilation)
nodes.role: Placed Brother Tiridates on Armenian Throne
nodes.notes: Preserved Zoroastrian Avestan texts and founded Vologesocerta.

nodes.name: King Artabanus IV / Ardawan (Last Parthian Shahanshah, d. 224 CE at Hormozdgan)
nodes.notes: Fell in battle against Ardashir I, ending the 470-year Arsacid Empire.

nodes.name: Aramaneak (Eldest Son of Hayk Nahapet)
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.12-15
nodes.notes: Settled in Ayrarat plain.

nodes.name: Aramayis (Son of Aramaneak; Builder of Armavir)
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.12-15
nodes.notes: Built capital Armavir on the Araxes.

nodes.name: Amasia (Son of Aramayis; Named Mt. Masis)
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.12-15
nodes.notes: Father of Gegham.

nodes.name: Gegham (Son of Amasia; Eponym of Lake Sevan / Gegharkunik)
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.12-15
nodes.notes: Father of Harma & Sisak (Syunik).

nodes.name: Harma (Son of Gegham)
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.12-15
nodes.notes: Father of Aram.

nodes.name: Patriarch Aram (Son of Harma; Classical Eponym of Armenia)
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.12-15
nodes.notes: Extended borders into Cappadocia and Assyria; father of Ara.

nodes.name: Ara the Handsome (Son of Aram; Coveted by Queen Semiramis)
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.12-15
nodes.notes: Fell defending Armenia against Semiramis (Shammuramat).

nodes.name: Ma'add ibn Adnan (Son of Adnan)
nodes.notes: Son of Adnan.

nodes.name: Nizar ibn Ma'add (Father of Mudar & Rabi'ah)
nodes.notes: Progenitor of the Nizarite Arab confederations.

nodes.name: Mudar ibn Nizar (Brother of Rabi'ah)
nodes.notes: Eponym of the Mudar tribes.

nodes.name: Ilyas ibn Mudar
nodes.notes: Married Khindif.

nodes.name: Mudrikah ('Amr) ibn Ilyas
nodes.notes: Son of Ilyas.

nodes.name: Khuzaymah ibn Mudrikah
nodes.notes: Father of Kinanah & Asad.

nodes.name: Kinanah ibn Khuzaymah
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Quraysh and allied Hijazi clans.

nodes.name: Al-Nadr ibn Kinanah
nodes.notes: Considered founder of Quraysh in some traditions.

nodes.name: Malik ibn al-Nadr
nodes.notes: Father of Fihr.

nodes.name: Fihr ibn Malik (Quraysh — Eponym of Tribe of Quraysh)
nodes.notes: United the Hijazi clans around Mecca as Quraysh.

nodes.name: Ghalib ibn Fihr
nodes.notes: Son of Fihr.

nodes.name: Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib
nodes.notes: Father of Ka'b.

nodes.name: Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy
nodes.notes: Preached at Mecca; father of Murrah & Adi (Umar's line).

nodes.name: Murrah ibn Ka'b
nodes.notes: Father of Kilab & Taym (Abu Bakr's clan).

nodes.name: Kilab ibn Murrah
nodes.notes: Married Fatimah bint Sa'd; father of Qusayy.

nodes.name: Qusayy ibn Kilab (Zayd — Unifier & Custodian of Mecca, c. 400–480 CE)
nodes.notes: Reclaimed custody of the Ka'bah and established Dar al-Nadwah in Mecca.

nodes.name: 'Abd Manaf ibn Qusayy (Al-Mughirah — Father of Hashim & 'Abd Shams)
nodes.role: 18th Gen Common Ancestor of Prophet, Umayyads & Abbasids
nodes.notes: Fathered twin lines: Hashim (Prophet, Alids, Abbasids) and 'Abd Shams (Umayyads).

nodes.name: Hashim ibn 'Abd Manaf ('Amr al-'Ula — Eponym of Banu Hashim, d. c. 497 CE)
nodes.notes: Led the winter & summer trade caravans of Quraysh; married Salma bint 'Amr of Medina.

nodes.name: 'Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim (Shaybah al-Hamd, c. 497–578 CE — Rediscovered Zamzam)
nodes.notes: Custodian of Mecca during the Year of the Elephant (570 CE); father of 'Abdallah, Abu Talib, Hamza & al-'Abbas.

nodes.name: 'Abdallah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib (545–570 CE; Father of Prophet Muhammad)
nodes.notes: Wed Aminah bint Wahb and passed away before Muhammad's birth.

nodes.name: Prophet Muhammad ibn 'Abdallah (570–632 CE; Seal of the Prophets in Islam)
nodes.role: Prophet of Islam & Unifier of Arabia
nodes.notes: Son of 'Abdallah & Aminah bint Wahb; married Khadijah bint Khuwaylid; father of Fatimah al-Zahra.

nodes.name: Fatimah al-Zahra bint Muhammad (c. 605–632 CE; Wife of Caliph Ali)
nodes.notes: Married cousin Ali ibn Abi Talib; mother of Imams Hasan and Husayn.

nodes.name: Imam al-Hasan ibn Ali (625–670 CE; Eldest Grandson of Prophet Muhammad)
nodes.notes: Father of Hasan al-Muthanna -> living Hashemites of Jordan & Alaouites of Morocco.

nodes.name: Aminah bint Wahb ibn 'Abd Manaf ibn Zuhrah (d. 577 CE; Mother of Prophet Muhammad)
nodes.notes: Noblewoman of Banu Zuhrah (descended from Kilab ibn Murrah); mother of Prophet Muhammad.

nodes.name: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (c. 555–619 CE; First Wife of Prophet Muhammad)
nodes.notes: Merchant of Quraysh (descended from Qusayy's brother 'Abd al-'Uzza); bore Fatimah al-Zahra.

nodes.name: Abu Talib ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib ('Abd Manaf, c. 535–619 CE; Uncle & Protector of Muhammad)
nodes.role: Chief of Banu Hashim & Father of Ali
nodes.notes: Father of Ja'far al-Tayyar and Caliph Ali ibn Abi Talib.

nodes.name: Imam al-Husayn ibn Ali (626–680 CE; Martyr of Karbala)
nodes.notes: Son of Ali & Fatimah; ancestor of Husaynid Sayyids and Nizari Ismaili Imams.

nodes.name: Imam Ali Zayn al-Abidin (659–713 CE; Son of Imam Husayn)
nodes.notes: Survived Karbala; father of Muhammad al-Baqir.

nodes.name: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (677–733 CE; Son of Zayn al-Abidin)
nodes.notes: Father of Ja'far al-Sadiq.

nodes.name: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (702–765 CE; Jurist & 6th Husaynid Imam)
nodes.role: Ancestor of Fatimids & Aga Khan V
nodes.notes: Teacher of Sunni & Shia jurists; father of Isma'il -> Fatimids -> Aga Khan V.

nodes.name: Al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib (c. 566–653 CE; Eponym of the Abbasid Caliphate)
nodes.role: Paternal Uncle of Muhammad & Progenitor of Abbasids
nodes.notes: Father of scholar 'Abdallah ibn al-'Abbas.

nodes.name: 'Abdallah ibn al-'Abbas (619–687 CE; Foremost Qur'anic Exegete & Grandfather of Caliphs)
nodes.notes: Grandfather of Abbasid caliphs al-Saffah and al-Mansur via Ali ibn 'Abdallah -> Muhammad.

nodes.name: Caliph Abu al-'Abbas al-Saffah (1st Abbasid Caliph, r. 750–754 CE)
nodes.notes: Brother of Caliph al-Mansur.

nodes.name: Caliph al-Mahdi (Son of al-Mansur; Father of Harun al-Rashid, r. 775–785 CE)
nodes.notes: Father of Caliphs al-Hadi and Harun al-Rashid.

nodes.name: 'Abd Shams ibn 'Abd Manaf (Progenitor of the Umayyad Caliphs)
nodes.role: Son of 'Abd Manaf & Twin Brother of Hashim
nodes.notes: Father of Umayyah.

nodes.name: Umayyah ibn 'Abd Shams (Eponym of Banu Umayyah)
nodes.notes: Father of Harb (Sufyanids) and Abu al-'As (Caliph Uthman & Marwanids).

nodes.name: Harb ibn Umayyah (Commander of Quraysh at Fijar)
nodes.notes: Father of Abu Sufyan.

nodes.name: Abu Sufyan Sakhr ibn Harb (c. 565–653 CE; Father of Mu'awiya I)
nodes.notes: Father of Caliph Mu'awiya I.

nodes.name: Caliph Yazid I ibn Mu'awiya (r. 680–683 CE)
nodes.notes: Son of Mu'awiya I.

nodes.name: Abu al-'As ibn Umayyah (Son of Umayyah; Ancestor of Uthman & Marwanids)
nodes.notes: Brother of Harb; ancestor of Caliph Uthman and the Marwanid Umayyad Caliphs of Damascus and Cordoba.

nodes.name: 'Affan ibn Abi al-'As (Father of Caliph Uthman)
nodes.notes: Father of 3rd Rashidun Caliph Uthman ibn 'Affan.

nodes.name: Al-Hakam ibn Abi al-'As (Brother of 'Affan; Father of Marwan I)
nodes.notes: Uncle of Caliph Uthman.

nodes.name: Caliph Marwan I ibn al-Hakam (623–685 CE; Founder of Marwanid Umayyads)
nodes.notes: Father of Caliph 'Abd al-Malik.

nodes.name: Caliph al-Walid I (r. 705–715 CE; Builder of Damascus Mosque & Expansion to Spain/Sindh)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of 'Abd al-Malik; under his reign Muslim armies reached Iberia & the Indus.

nodes.name: Caliph Hisham ibn 'Abd al-Malik (r. 724–743 CE; Grandfather of 'Abd al-Rahman I)
nodes.notes: Son of 'Abd al-Malik; grandfather of Emir 'Abd al-Rahman I of Cordoba via Mu'awiya ibn Hisham.

nodes.name: King Ya'rub ibn Qahtan (1st Arabic-Speaking King of Yemen)
nodes.era: Proto-Arabian Era (Tabari; Caussin de Perceval Vol. 1)
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Yemeni & South Arabian Arabized tribes.

nodes.name: Yashjub ibn Ya'rub
nodes.notes: Son of Ya'rub.

nodes.name: Saba ibn Yashjub ('Abd Shams — Builder of Marib Dam)
nodes.role: Eponym of Sabaeans; Father of Himyar & Kahlan
nodes.notes: Fathered twin branches Himyar (Tubba kings) and Kahlan (Lakhmids, Ghassanids & Azd).

nodes.name: Himyar ibn Saba (Eponym of Himyarite Kingdom of Yemen)
nodes.notes: Eponym of the Himyarite Tubba monarchs.

nodes.name: Tubba As'ad Abu Karib of Himyar (c. 390–440 CE; Embraced Judaism in Yathrib)
nodes.notes: Adopted Judaism in Yathrib and clothed the Ka'bah.

nodes.name: King Yusuf As'ar Dhu-Nuwas of Himyar (r. 517–525 CE; Clashed with King Kaleb of Aksum)
nodes.role: Last Independent Jewish Tubba of Himyar
nodes.notes: Defeated at the Red Sea by Aksumite King Kaleb (Elesbaan) in 525 CE.

nodes.name: Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan (Restorer of Himyar against Aksum, c. 575 CE)
nodes.notes: Reclaimed Yemen from Aksumite rule.

nodes.name: Kahlan ibn Saba (Brother of Himyar; Ancestor of Lakhmids, Ghassanids & Ansar of Medina)
nodes.notes: Son of Saba; ancestral trunk of the Lakhmid kings of Al-Hirah and Ghassanid kings of Syria.

nodes.name: Jafnah ibn 'Amr (1st Ghassanid King of Syria, c. 220 CE)
nodes.notes: Founded the Arab Christian Jafnid/Ghassanid kingdom allied with Rome/Byzantium.

nodes.name: King al-Harith V ibn Jabalah of Ghassan (Arethas, r. 529–569 CE; Ally of Justinian I)
nodes.role: Patricius & Paramount Phylarch of the Arabs
nodes.notes: Elevated by Byzantine Emperor Justinian I to king over Syria's Arab foederati.

nodes.name: King Imru' al-Qays I ibn 'Amr of Al-Hirah (d. 328 CE; Namara Inscription)
nodes.notes: Attested in the 328 CE Namara inscription — oldest dated classical Arabic royal epitaph.

nodes.name: King al-Mundhir III ibn al-Nu'man of Al-Hirah (r. 505–554 CE)
nodes.notes: Fought Roman-allied Ghassanid King al-Harith V across Syria.

nodes.name: King al-Nu'man III ibn al-Mundhir of Al-Hirah (r. 582–602 CE)
nodes.role: Last Christian Lakhmid King of Al-Hirah
nodes.notes: Patron of Pre-Islamic Arabic poets; executed by Khosrow II Parviz, sparking the Battle of Dhu Qar.

nodes.name: King Septimius Odaenathus of Palmyra (Husband of Zenobia, d. 267 CE)
nodes.role: Corrector Totius Orientis & King of Kings of Palmyra
nodes.notes: Defeated Shapur I of Persia after Valerian's capture; husband of Zenobia.

nodes.name: Empress Zenobia / Bat-Zabbai of Palmyra (r. 267–272 CE)
nodes.notes: Ruled Syria, Egypt, and Anatolia; claimed descent from Cleopatra VII of Egypt and Dido of Carthage.

nodes.name: Emperor Vaballathus of Palmyra (Son of Odaenathus & Zenobia, r. 267–272 CE)
nodes.notes: Bore titles of Augustus until defeated by Roman Emperor Aurelian in 272 CE.

nodes.name: Berr / Mazigh (Patriarch of the Imazighen in Ibn Khaldun)
nodes.era: Ibn Khaldun Histoire des Berberes v4
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Bernes (Branes) and Madghis al-Abtar (Botr).

nodes.name: Bernes (Progenitor of Sanhaja, Masmuda & Kutama Berbers)
nodes.notes: Father of the great sedentary Amazigh confederations.

nodes.name: Sanhaja (Son of Bernes; Ancestor of Almoravids & Zirids)
nodes.notes: Forebear of the Sahara and Maghreb Sanhaja confederations.

nodes.name: Masmuda (Son of Bernes; Ancestor of Atlas Almohads)
nodes.notes: Forebear of the High Atlas Masmuda tribes.

nodes.name: Kutama (Son of Bernes; Supporters of Fatimid North Africa)
nodes.notes: Kabyle confederation key to North African state formation.

nodes.name: Madghis al-Abtar (Progenitor of Zenata, Luwata & Hawwara Berbers)
nodes.notes: Progenitor of the Zenata nomadic confederations.

nodes.name: Zana / Zenata (Descendant of Madghis al-Abtar; Ancestor of Marinids & Zayyanids)
nodes.notes: Progenitor of Queen al-Kahina's Jerawa Zenata tribe.

nodes.name: King Kusayla / Aksil of Altava (d. 688 CE; Awraba Berber Monarch)
nodes.notes: United Amazigh and Byzantine forces in Numidia.

nodes.name: Queen Dihya al-Kahina (d. 703 CE; Jerawa Zenata Queen of the Aures)
nodes.notes: Jerawa Zenata queen who led Amazigh resistance in the Aures Mountains.
